title: Want cheaper flights? Google says this is the best time to book one
summary: Cheap flights care more about timing than Tuesdays.
body: TL;DR Google says domestic flights have historically been cheapest around 39 days before departure, while international fares hit their lowest around 89 days out. The idea that Tuesday is the best day to book is largely a myth, with the cheapest booking day saving only about 1.4% versus the most expensive. Changing when and how you fly matters more: weekday travel can save up to 20% domestically, while nonstop flights cost around 20% more than connecting options. Booking a flight can sometimes feel like a gamble. You find a fare that looks reasonable, but instead of booking it, you start wondering whether it’ll be cheaper tomorrow. But wait too long, and you could end up paying even more. Google already tries to make that decision easier with its travel tools, and now it’s sharing more data on when to book. If you already know your destination and travel dates, Google Flights and AI Mode in Search can show you the “cheapest time to book,” helping you understand whether current fares are on the lower side or if prices could change in the coming days.

title: GrapheneOS explains why your Pixel is lagging and freezing after Android 17 QPR1
summary: A newly identified regression could explain some of the lag Pixel users reported.
body: TL;DR Some Pixel owners reported worse performance after installing September’s Android 17 QPR1 update. GrapheneOS says it has found a regression in the update that can cause lag, stuttering, freezes, and app crashes under memory pressure. While GrapheneOS has already patched the problem, stock Pixel users are still waiting for Google to release a fix. Android 17 QPR1 was supposed to improve Pixel phones, but for a noticeable number of owners, the September update seems to have had the opposite effect. We recently asked Android Authority readers how their Pixels were behaving after installing the update , and performance problems stood out as the most common complaint among those who reported new issues. Now, GrapheneOS may have finally found the reason for at least some of that slowdown. The privacy-focused project says it has identified a regression introduced with Android 17 QPR1 that can cause Pixel phones to stutter, lag, or even freeze when memory is under pressure. In more severe cases, affected processes can reportedly be terminated after becoming unresponsive.

Ed-tech company Chegg filed an antitrust lawsuit against Google last year over AI Overviews and how the feature was affecting website traffic and affiliate revenues. Publisher Penske Media Corporation, known for publications like Billboard , Variety , and Rolling Stone , later filed its own lawsuit against the search giant .
